rationale: PROGRESSION-smg1-04-01 flagged i2, i3, k2, ch1, all colliding with anchor k1 on template 'set the clock to show #:#.'. i2 (10:00) and k2 (5:00) are ordinary G1 fluency reps of the plain on-the-hour skill at different hours; i3 (12:00) is the noon/midnight both-hands-overlap edge case its own preceding concept card c3 explicitly teaches -- all three legitimate, left untouched. ch1 (11:00) was the genuine miss: as the challenge tier it posed the identical clockSet construct action as k1/i2/k2 with no distinguishing content, and its old hourFeedback's near-12 hint was never actually exercised by the clockSet widget (which only grades final hand placement). REDESIGNED ch1: changed the action from CONSTRUCT (drag hands to a given digital time) to READ/IDENTIFY (given a described hand position in words, select the correct time from four options), turning the near-12 hint into a real distractor -- new prompt 'The hour hand points to 11 and the minute hand points to 12. What time is it?', correct 11:00, traps 12:00 (rounds the near-boundary hour hand up to the next number), 12:11 (swaps which hand supplies the hour vs the \":00\" reading), and 10:00 (off-by-one the other direction). This is a genuinely different question job (recognize/read vs. manipulate/construct) targeting a misconception the original widget shape could never surface. No variant field existed on ch1 before or after this edit; no shared generator file was touched. Siblings i2/i3/k2 remain live-detected as repeating k1's template by design (fluency practice cannot and should not clear this structural detector) and are honestly left open.
reopenCondition: Reopen if step ch1 in smg1-04-01 reverts to a prompt whose normalized template again matches a sibling step's, or if its widget/prompt/answer changes again without re-verifying the redesign still resolves distinctly from k1/i2/i3/k2.
